title: Systemd fails to mount LVM swap when initrd without systemd
body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

255

### Used distribution

Fedora, Debian, Ubuntu, Gentoo

### Linux kernel version used

various

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemctl, systemd

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

Swap is mounted, the system boots

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

systemd hangs looking for the udev device path for the lvm mount, even though it's mapped, and in the fstab. The swap is not activated

### Steps to reproduce the problem

boot without udev, mount lvm volumes using lvm tools.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> udevd is necessary in initrd to support such setup.

I don't see why? it works fine without it, other than systemd failing to find the /dev/disk uuid.

I'm basing this on the debian/fedora installers which add fstab entries for the swap.

There is no reason for me to include udev in my system as it doesn't need anything dynamic.

Is there some way systemd could see udev was not used pre-boot and accommodate?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
- Is sysroot also on LVM? Or, only swap is on LVM?
- Is udevd disabled only in initrd phase?
- boot process hang in initrd phase? Or after switching root?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
fstab is converted to systemd .mount and .swap units in both initrd phase and after switching root. And, starting swap unit requires underlying device is processed by udevd.

Maybe, we should add `rd.systemd.swap=BOOL` kernel command line option to allow delaying configuring swap in initrd.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> * Is sysroot also on LVM? Or, only swap is on LVM?
> 
>     * Is udevd disabled only in initrd phase?
> 
>     * boot process hang in initrd phase? Or after switching root?
> 
> 
> Please provide the fstab file.

This disk layout is the default made for the "encrypted" setup in the debian installer, I'm using it as a reference.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6275f12-dbd1-46c2-b98d-035aef14adaa)

The initrd works fine, the system I made autodetects LUKS/LVM stuff: https://github.com/reporter/ugrd

The issue is that after it does a switch_root and passes things off to systemd, it stalls and I have to manually mount the swap. This issue seems to only occur when LVM swap is used.

I don't typically use systemd, so I'm not sure how those units are created/used, but my intrd system makes a simple bash script to mount things, and it works properly. The "issue" is that it does not use udev, and I think systemd is timing out looking for udev device nodes, when those are not made. I think if something re-triggerd udev shortly after systemd init's, that could fix things. I just don't think it makes sense to add udev to an initramfs, when it's only a systemd requirement, and `swapon -a` works fine without that. It seems like an added check that only causes problems. I can understand preferring udev device ids, but if `swapon -a` works, why do more?

it is not, the initrd ignores the swap. it exists only to get the rootfs mounted, and switch root. I could make it mount lvm swap stuff, but i think it makes more sense to let the main init system do that, if it can.

I'm trying to adhere strictly to the design philosophy of "the initramfs exists to mount the rootfs", no more, no less. It currently has mechanisms for mounting the swap, but they have to be manually configure by the user. I think the best user experience is one where the initramfs has a simple purpose and there is not confusion about where things are initialized. It should be clear that the main init system sets up most of your fstab stuff, and swap, and that your initramfs does it if you explicitly tell it to. I think it's a bug that systemd has a hard requirement that lvm stuff is setup with udev pre-boot, especially when `swapon -a` works.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hm, for some reasons, udevd does not add symlink `/dev/mapper/$env{DM_NAME}`. Hence, PID1 handles that the block device is not ready, and the swap unit and all units which depend on the swap are stuck.

So, this is not an issue in systemd or udevd, but should be caused by the LVM project, as the udev rules for LVM volume is provided by the LVM project. Please open a new issue at https://github.com/lvmteam/lvm2 with linking with this issue page.

Note, of course, a workaround for the issue is setting `noauto` option to the swap volume in fstab, and calling `swapon` manually.

Closing.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I guess, the scenario that causes the issue is something like the following:
1. The lvm volumes are activated without udevd (in initrd, right?), and somehow symlinks /dev/mapper/xxx are created.
2. After switching root, PID1 labels that these block devices are not ready, as udevd not processed them yet.
3. udevd processes the LVM volumes, but for some reasons, the corresponding rules do not request the symlinks.
4. udevd notifies the LVM volumes (dm-x) are ready, but the notifications do not contain about symlinks /dev/mapper/xxx.
5. PID1 still handles /dev/mapper/xxx are not ready yet.

If the above story is correct, the issue should be in the initrd script you use and udev rules provided by LVM.

> I guess, the scenario that causes the issue is something like the following:
> 
>     1. The lvm volumes are activated without udevd (in initrd, right?), and somehow symlinks /dev/mapper/xxx are created.

I think the symlinks are created because my system runs `vgscan --mknodes`. This was an attempt to try to add the nodes to appease systemd, and this did not work. I left it in because it doesn't seem to harm anything, and I think having the mapped entries makes sense.
>

This is my guess as well, it seems it's waiting for udev to add these nodes. It doesn't seem to make the nodes if `vgscan --mknodes` is not used, but still fails. My guess is because it has a hard expectation that udev makes these.
>     3. udevd processes the LVM volumes, but for some reasons, the corresponding rules do not request the symlinks.
> 
FWIW hardlinks are made, or they are converted to hardlinks after switch_root. Not sure how much this matters, but the entries in  /dev/mapper seem totally valid in this form.
>     4. udevd notifies the LVM volumes (dm-x) are ready, but the notifications do not contain about symlinks /dev/mapper/xxx.
> 
>     5. PID1 still handles /dev/mapper/xxx are not ready yet.
> 
Yes, even though the devices are present, some wires are crossed and it's not recognizing them
> 
> If the above story is correct, the issue should be in the initrd script you use and udev rules provided by LVM.

I don't think it makes sense for the initrd to use udev for the sole purpose of making systemd happy _after the initramfs is gone_. The initramfs itself does not need udev, and mounts the root fine without it.

The reason why the swap is not enabled by systemd is that the underlying device is not correctly processed by udevd. I have no idea what udev rules provided by LVM and device-mapper do. The issue should be solved by the provider of the rules.

https://github.com/lvmteam/lvm2/issues/153#issuecomment-2268485407

It seems to be a deficiency with udev, or at least a complication from design limits. I'm not sure how I would "record and replay" events but that seems quite complicated, and seems like something udev should be able to do.

`ugrd.fs.fakeudev` as you found out, but for anyone who finds this issue.

In its current state, systemd requires udev is running before any dm mounts are made. Alternatively, lvm tools can be built without udev support which should cause this to be a non-issue? I have not tested that option but it doesn't really seem like a solution. If this doesn't happen something must make "fake" (or real) udev entries describing those mounts or systemd won't see them once it starts. If systemd doesn't see these udev data, the mounts may as well not exist.
